analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the speaker, לוֹ identifies Cain as the addressee, and לָכֵן begins the words spoken.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ יַהְוֶה, “Yahweh said to him,” יַהְוֶה names the speaker and is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר. The pronoun לוֹ refers to Cain, whom Yahweh addresses.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: לָכֵן introduces Yahweh’s response to Cain’s fear of being killed. The clause that follows declares that anyone who kills Cain will face sevenfold vengeance.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לָ־ prefixed to the adverb כֵּן.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל הֹרֵג קַיִן, כָּל quantifies the singular participle הֹרֵג, yielding “anyone who kills Cain.” The threat of sevenfold vengeance applies to each potential killer.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל הֹרֵג קַיִן means “anyone who kills Cain.” The participle denotes the person who would do the killing, and קַיִן names the one who would be killed.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct

draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל הֹרֵג קַיִן, “anyone who kills Cain,” קַיִן names the person threatened. Later in the verse, YHWH gives Cain a sign to keep anyone who finds him from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix. It is the object of the participle הֹרֵג.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

analysis.evidence: In שִׁבְעָתַיִם יֻקָּם, שִׁבְעָתַיִם modifies the passive verb יֻקָּם and specifies the measure of vengeance for killing Cain.
analysis.morphology: Feminine dual absolute numeral form used adverbially.

analysis.evidence: כָּל הֹרֵג קַיִן identifies the potential killer of Cain, and שִׁבְעָתַיִם specifies the measure of retribution. Together with יֻקָּם, the warning means that sevenfold vengeance will be exacted for killing Cain. The following clause says that YHWH gave Cain a sign to keep anyone who found him from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Hophal imperfect, third-person masculine singular. The root-initial נ assimilates to ק, marked by the dagesh. No attached particle or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject, אוֹת is the sign he set, and לְקַיִן identifies Cain as the person for whom he set it. The purpose clause explains that the sign was to keep anyone who found Cain from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׂם יַהְוֶה לְקַיִן אוֹת, יַהְוֶה is the subject of וַיָּשֶׂם ‘set’. Yahweh sets a sign for Cain to keep anyone who finds him from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׂם יַהְוֶה לְקַיִן אוֹת, לְ marks Cain as the person for whom YHWH sets a sign. The phrase לְבִלְתִּי הַכּוֹת אֹתוֹ explains its purpose, to keep anyone who finds Cain from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine singular personal name.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

analysis.evidence: אוֹת is the direct object of וַיָּשֶׂם. YHWH set a sign for Cain (לְקַיִן) so that anyone who found him would refrain from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, without prefix or suffix. Gender is unmarked here.

analysis.evidence: YHWH gives Cain a sign. In לְבִלְתִּי הַכּוֹת אֹתוֹ כָּל־מֹצְאוֹ, אֹתוֹ refers to Cain and כָּל־מֹצְאוֹ is the subject of הַכּוֹת. The sign serves to keep anyone who finds Cain from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Negative particle with prefixed לְ, introducing the infinitive construct הַכּוֹת in a purpose clause.
analysis.sense: Negates the action that the sign is intended to prevent.

analysis.evidence: לְבִלְתִּי negates הַכּוֹת. Its object אֹתוֹ refers to Cain, and its subject כָּל מֹצְאוֹ means “anyone who finds him.” The earlier phrase כָּל הֹרֵג קַיִן (“anyone who kills Cain”) identifies the fatal act the sign is meant to prevent.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct, without a suffix

draft.change: Add Gen.4.15 as an example of the existing object-pronoun sense in et.
draft.definition: With a pronominal suffix, אֵת expresses the direct object as a pronoun separate from the verb.
draft.evidence: In Gen.4.15, הַכּוֹת אֹתוֹ means ‘to strike him.’ The suffix refers to Cain.

analysis.evidence: In לְבִלְתִּי הַכּוֹת אֹתוֹ כָּל מֹצְאוֹ, ‘so that no one who found him would strike him,’ כָּל מֹצְאוֹ identifies the potential striker. אֹתוֹ identifies Cain, just named in לְקַיִן, as the person who would receive the blow.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in its suffixed form אֹת־ with the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: In לְבִלְתִּי הַכּוֹת אֹתוֹ כָּל מֹצְאוֹ, כָּל quantifies the singular participle מֹצְאוֹ, ‘one who finds him’. The sign keeps anyone who finds Cain from striking him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל מֹצְאוֹ means “anyone who finds him.” The sign given to Cain is to prevent such a person from striking him. The suffix on מֹצְאוֹ refers to Cain, as does אֹתוֹ after הַכּוֹת.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, with a third-person masculine singular object suffix referring to Cain.
